Scenario Name: Price computation is correct across cart size variations (1, 2, 6 items)
Probable Root Cause: Automation defect. The saved error-context.md confirms the actual failure is InventoryPage.addProductToCart('Sauce Labs Backpack') timing out on the "Add to cart" button locator; the page snapshot shows the badge already at '1' and Backpack's button already toggled to 'Remove', because the '1 item' test.step already added it and the loop reuses the same `page`/session across the '1 item', '2 items' and '6 items' test.step iterations in reachCheckoutStepOne() without ever clearing the cart, so the later iteration's re-add of the same product hangs forever waiting for an 'Add to cart' button that no longer exists.

Probable Root Cause: Application defect. The item itself remains in the cart (badge still '1', Backpack shows 'Remove' in the post-failure snapshot) so 'items intact' holds, but the destination page contradicts the explicit acceptance criterion in TestCases/JIRA-190_TestDesign.csv's TS-8/POS-8 rows ("User is returned to /cart.html"), which carry no noted Key Gap - i.e. this destination was a firm, unambiguous requirement.
Suggested Fix: File a defect against the Cancel button on checkout-step-two.html: it routes to /inventory.html instead of the specified /cart.html. Have product/dev confirm whether the app's routing should change to match TS-8/POS-8, or whether the requirement's documented destination should be corrected to match actual (and apparently long-standing) SauceDemo behavior - either way this is a spec-vs-app mismatch, not a locator/assertion bug.

Scenario Name: Whitespace-only input in required shipping fields is rejected
Error Log: Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed Locator: getByTestId('error') Expected: visible
Probable Root Cause: Requirement ambiguity. The saved error-context.md confirms the app silently accepted firstName='   ' (three spaces) as valid and advanced straight to checkout-step-two.html (Item total $29.99, Finish button rendered) instead of showing the 'first name is required' error CheckoutStepOnePage.expectValidationError() waited for. The test's own inline comment says this exact outcome 'may surface a real defect if SauceDemo treats whitespace as non-empty input' but explicitly flags that 'current app behavior for whitespace-only trimming is unverified by the requirement' - i.e. the pass/fail bar here was an assumption the requirement never actually specified.
Suggested Fix: Get product-owner confirmation on the missing acceptance criterion: should whitespace-only input in required shipping fields be trimmed and rejected as blank, or is any non-empty string (including whitespace) acceptable? Update TestDesign/TestCases and this assertion to match once decided, rather than treating the current mismatch as a confirmed code defect.

Scenario Name: Direct URL navigation to checkout-complete.html without completing prior steps
Error Log: Error: expect(locator).not.toHaveText(expected) failed Locator: getByTestId('complete-header') Expected pattern: not /thank you for your order/i
Probable Root Cause: Application defect. The saved error-context.md confirms navigating directly to /checkout-complete.html after login (with no items added and no checkout steps completed) renders the real 'Thank you for your order!' heading exactly as if a genuine order had been placed, with no redirect/guard - precisely the false-confirmation behavior EDGE-9's requirement explicitly says must not happen ("does not falsely display 'Thank You for your order!' for a non-existent order").
Suggested Fix: File a defect: checkout-complete.html has no guard against direct/unauthenticated-order navigation and always renders the static order-confirmation content regardless of whether checkout was actually completed. This is a customer-trust risk (a user could believe a non-existent order was placed) and should be prioritized for a server-side or client-side state check before the confirmation page renders.
